stem: In a study with complete follow-up, 40 of 200 participants in group X and 20 of 400 participants in group Y develop the same outcome. A report originally compares X with Y, but the investigator now wants Y compared with X. Which of the following pairs uses the requested reference group?

options.label: A
options.text: Risk ratio 0.5; Y has half the outcome risk of X
options.explanation: Dividing the case counts alone gives 20/40 but ignores the different group sizes. The requested ratio compares risks of 20/400 and 40/200, rather than the numbers of cases.
options.misconception: Compares raw case counts without adjusting for unequal group sizes.

options.label: B
options.text: Risk ratio 0.25; Y has one-quarter the outcome risk of X
options.explanation: Group Y has risk 20/400, or 5%, and group X has risk 40/200, or 20%. Comparing Y with X gives 0.05/0.20 = 0.25, one-quarter the risk.
options.misconception: No misconception: the requested Y-to-X comparison divides 5% by 20%.

options.label: C
options.text: Risk ratio 2.0; Y has twice the outcome risk of X
options.explanation: Two is the ratio of the raw case counts in the opposite direction. Both the specified direction and the different group sizes must be reflected in the risk calculation.
options.misconception: Reverses the requested direction and compares case counts instead of risks.

options.label: D
options.text: Risk ratio 4.0; Y has four times the outcome risk of X
options.explanation: Four is the risk ratio for X compared with Y. Reversing the comparison makes X the denominator, so the requested ratio is the reciprocal, 0.25.
options.misconception: Reports the X-to-Y ratio when the requested numerator is group Y.

options.label: E
options.text: Risk ratio 1.0; Y has the same outcome risk as X
options.explanation: The group-specific risks differ: 5% in Y and 20% in X. A ratio of one would require equal risks, which these observed counts and denominators do not show.
options.misconception: Assumes equal risks despite different group-specific case fractions.

context:
Learning objective: Match the numerator and reference group to the requested direction of a risk comparison.

Group Y has risk 20/400, or 5%, and group X has risk 40/200, or 20%. Comparing Y with X gives 0.05/0.20 = 0.25, one-quarter the risk.
